newsitem.title: CHINA: China seeks Newmont, Broken Hill gold mine reports.
newsitem.headline: China seeks Newmont, Broken Hill gold mine reports.

text.p: China has told U.S. firm Newmont Gold and Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd to submit feasability reports for a cooperative gold mine project, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The China National Gold Corp (CNGC) would compare the reports to see which company it preferred for involvement in the Lannigou mine in the southwestern province of Guizhou, the newspaper said.
The CNGC had discovered proven reserves of 60 tonnes of gold in the Lannigou's main vein, it said.

Even though the Chinese firm would express a preference for one foreign company, both candidates should remain involved in the project because the situation could change, it quoted an unnamed CNGC official as saying without giving more details.

Both Newmont and Broken Hill have expressed interest in exploring and exploiting the area around the Lannigou mine, but there was still insufficient information on the area for a descision to be made, it said.

Chinese officials have said that poor profit prospects from gold mining are likely to deter foreign companies from investing in the industry, despite the signing of China's first gold mining joint venture.
China's Zhaoyuan Gold Industrial Group and Cananda's Asia Minerals Corp this month signed a $75 million, 50-50 deal to develop the Yinggezhuang min in eastern Shandong province.
